\nRelease notes\n

Sourced from jsdom's releases.

\n
\n

v31.0.0

\n

Breaking changes

\n
    \n
  • Changed the optional canvas and image decoding backend from canvas to @napi-rs/canvas. Install @napi-rs/canvas v1.0.13 or later in the v1.x series alongside jsdom; installing canvas alone no longer enables this support. The new backend provides prebuilt Skia binaries on supported platforms, and rendering and encoded image bytes can differ. Projects using native canvas objects or custom font registration should follow the canvas migration guidance. Added WebP serialization through canvas.toDataURL() and canvas.toBlob(). Fixed image loading to wait for decoding before firing load, discard obsolete source requests, avoid refetching when dimensions change, and prevent failed images from drawing stale contents. Fixed canvas context and serialization behavior, including unsupported context types, read-only ctx.canvas, image-drawing exceptions, MIME type and quality normalization, and asynchronous null results from canvas.toBlob() for empty canvases or encoding failures. (@​Brooooooklyn)
    • \n
  • Changed CSS parsing, selector matching, and computed styles to use a new integrated implementation, with substantially expanded support and faster selector queries and repeated style reads. This includes cascade layers, nesting, @scope, custom-property substitution and registration through @property and CSS.registerProperty(), typed attr(), conditional if(), shadow-tree styling with :host, ::slotted(), and ::part(), pseudo-element computed styles, and constructable stylesheets with document.adoptedStyleSheets and shadowRoot.adoptedStyleSheets. Fixed numerous cascade, shorthand, serialization, and default-style issues; computed declarations now stay live across DOM and stylesheet changes. CSS serialization and computed values can differ from previous releases.
    • \n
  • Changed HTML and XML parsing to pause at blocking scripts until their required resources are ready. The JSDOM constructor, JSDOM.fromURL(), and JSDOM.fromFile() can now return partially parsed documents. Wait for DOMContentLoaded for the finished tree, or the window's load event for load-delaying resources, checking document.readyState first in case the event has already fired. XML syntax errors encountered after asynchronous parsing resumes are reported through the virtual console as "xml-parsing" errors.
    • \n
\n

Other changes

\n
    \n
  • Added window.reportError(), which dispatches an error event and reports uncanceled errors to the virtual console. (@​sarankumar1325)
    • \n
  • Added element.ariaBrailleLabel and element.ariaBrailleRoleDescription. (@​Kjubikstronk)
    • \n
  • Fixed page-completion load events to fire only on the window. Use window.addEventListener("load", ...) or window.onload instead of listening on the document.
    • \n
  • Fixed document.open(), including implicit calls from document.write(), to clear event listeners and handlers from the document, its descendants, and its window when replacing the input stream.
    • \n
  • Fixed document.write() to process successive writes through the parser's input stream, preserve insertion points across nested scripts, and make completed text immediately visible. Script-created input streams now remain open until document.close().
    • \n
  • Fixed dynamically inserted scripts to respect script.async = false execution order, use their source text and document from preparation time, and avoid executing after adoption into another document. Scripts parsed through inert fragment APIs no longer execute when subsequently inserted.
    • \n
  • Fixed unrelated images, stylesheets, and frames being delayed behind scripts, and resource completion events firing before nested stylesheet imports finish. Cyclic imports no longer prevent completion, and <style> elements in shadow trees now fire load events.
    • \n
  • Fixed window.stop() to cancel pending subresource and XMLHttpRequest requests in descendant frames and suppress completion events for canceled loads, while allowing subsequent requests to proceed.
    • \n
  • Fixed repeated document.close() calls replaying readiness and load events, and incorrect iframe load events when reopening documents from event handlers.
    • \n
  • Fixed memory leaks where pending request interceptor promises retained closed windows, introduced in v28.0.0.
    • \n
  • Fixed focus remaining on elements that become non-focusable after DOM or style changes. Focus now moves asynchronously to the document's viewport, and element.blur() can release it immediately.
    • \n
  • Fixed document.hasFocus() returning false before an element is focused or during focus transitions within the document, including inside frames.
    • \n
  • Fixed \\<template> parsing and template.innerHTML serialization in XML documents, including templates with namespace prefixes. (@​b84330808)
    • \n
  • Fixed rect.toJSON() and performance.toJSON() to create their result objects in the method's realm instead of the host Node.js realm.
    • \n
\n
\n
\n

  • 825fa8e 31.0.0

  • 9f2e49a Add ariaBrailleLabel and ariaBrailleRoleDescription
    • \n
  • 4c0a35e Flush text written with document.write()
    • \n
  • fce11d3 Switch canvas support to @​napi-rs/canvas
    • \n
  • 27614bf Fix document.hasFocus() during focus changes
    • \n
  • 627ade2 Implement asynchronous focus fixup
    • \n
  • 8bd17a2 Implement reportError()
    • \n
  • 5ae66cf Update webidl2js and remove IDL workarounds
    • \n
  • ce5a100 Align development scripts and CI
    • \n
  • 9cc717f Adopt ESLint config v6 and oxfmt
    • \n
  • Additional commits viewable in compare view

  • Added element.ariaBrailleLabel and element.ariaBrailleRoleDescription. (@​Kjubikstronk)
    • \n
  • Fixed page-completion load events to fire only on the window. Use window.addEventListener("load", ...) or window.onload instead of listening on the document.
    • \n
  • Fixed document.open(), including implicit calls from document.write(), to clear event listeners and handlers from the document, its descendants, and its window when replacing the input stream.
    • \n
  • Fixed document.write() to process successive writes through the parser's input stream, preserve insertion points across nested scripts, and make completed text immediately visible. Script-created input streams now remain open until document.close().
    • \n
  • Fixed dynamically inserted scripts to respect script.async = false execution order, use their source text and document from preparation time, and avoid executing after adoption into another document. Scripts parsed through inert fragment APIs no longer execute when subsequently inserted.
    • \n
  • Fixed unrelated images, stylesheets, and frames being delayed behind scripts, and resource completion events firing before nested stylesheet imports finish. Cyclic imports no longer prevent completion, and <style> elements in shadow trees now fire load events.
    • \n
  • Fixed window.stop() to cancel pending subresource and XMLHttpRequest requests in descendant frames and suppress completion events for canceled loads, while allowing subsequent requests to proceed.
    • \n
  • Fixed repeated document.close() calls replaying readiness and load events, and incorrect iframe load events when reopening documents from event handlers.
    • \n
  • Fixed memory leaks where pending request interceptor promises retained closed windows, introduced in v28.0.0.
    • \n
  • Fixed focus remaining on elements that become non-focusable after DOM or style changes. Focus now moves asynchronously to the document's viewport, and element.blur() can release it immediately.
    • \n
  • Fixed document.hasFocus() returning false before an element is focused or during focus transitions within the document, including inside frames.
    • \n
  • Fixed \\<template> parsing and template.innerHTML serialization in XML documents, including templates with namespace prefixes. (@​b84330808)
    • \n
  • Fixed rect.toJSON() and performance.toJSON() to create their result objects in the method's realm instead of the host Node.js realm.

**当前有两个问题：一次证据上传故障，以及只重跑失败分片与证据收集规则不兼容。没有发现本轮测试断言失败。**

1. **首轮真正失败在上传阶段。**  
   macOS 第 4 分片的 84 个测试全部通过，进程退出码为 0，清理已验证。随后上传必需证据时出现：
   ```
   Failed to CreateArtifact: Unable to make request: ENOTFOUND
   ```
   约 24 秒后，另一个原始报告上传成功。因此，证据支持短暂的 DNS／网络故障；不能据此断言 GitHub 服务整体故障，也不能归因于产品代码。

2. **上传失败导致后续验收连锁失败。**  
   第 4 分片被标记失败 → macOS 汇总为 failure → Chromium 证据收集器拒绝验收 → 最终 UI 检查失败。  
   即使该分片没有 portable 用例，它的完整性清单仍是必需证据，不能省略。

3. **第二轮仅重跑第 4 分片，无法补齐当前规则要求的证据。**  
   工作流只下载当前 `run_attempt` 的文件；收集代码还要求 Linux 4 份、macOS 8 份、Windows 4 份清单全部匹配同一 attempt。现在其他分片保留的是第 1 轮文件，第 4 分片将生成第 2 轮文件。**按现有代码，即使第 4 分片通过，收集器仍会因缺少其余第 2 轮文件失败。**

   这是 CI 恢复机制的限制：普通“仅重跑失败任务”不能满足这里的严格证据协议，也放大了一次上传故障的恢复成本。

**当前可靠的恢复方式是：本轮结束后，完整重跑 UI 工作流一次，生成同一轮的完整证据。其他已通过的工作流无需重跑，也无需修改产品代码或降低验收要求。**

另外，我之前把“不是当前会话触发”直接描述成“另一个会话在操作”，推断过头了。GitHub 只能证明 `Kingson4Wu` 凭据触发了重跑，不能区分网页点击、脚本或其他会话。这不应成为停止分析的理由。

Original: “什么问题，分析一下啊”  
Better: “Analyze the failure and explain the root cause.”  
Why: 明确要求分析失败机制，而非仅汇报状态。  
Pattern: “Distinguish the original failure from downstream failures.”  
Collocations: root cause, downstream failure, recovery procedure  
IPA: analyze /ˈænəlaɪz/

刚查到第 2 轮最终结果：

| 环节 | 结果 |
|---|---|
| macOS 第 4 分片测试及上传 | ✅ 成功 |

| 整轮 UI 工作流 | ❌ 已结束，失败 |

汇总日志明确报错：
```text
ENOENT: chromium-portable-ubuntu-24.04-1-2
```

原因是：**GitHub 复用了其他分片第 1 轮的成功状态，但我们的收集器只读取第 2 轮文件。** 所以页面上测试任务都是绿色，最后汇总仍然失败。这次已由实际日志证实，不再只是代码推断。[查看第 2 轮结果](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/actions/runs/42623416724/attempts/2)

当前问题在 **CI 的局部重跑兼容性**。完整重跑 UI 工作流可以按现有规则恢复；长期优化则应让收集器在严格验证来源后复用成功分片证据，避免一次上传故障迫使全部测试重跑。

Better: “Isn’t the rerun progressing normally?”  
Why: “Progressing normally” 描述运行过程，不代表最终通过。  
Pattern: “The shard passed, but evidence collection failed.”

jobs:
  platform:
    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    name: Portable checks (${{ matrix.os }})
    runs-on: ${{ (inputs.full || 'true') == 'true' && matrix.os || 'ubuntu-latest' }}
    timeout-minutes: 25
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-26-intel, windows-latest]
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 2
      - id: scope
        uses: ./.github/actions/ci-scope
        with:
          full: ${{ (inputs.full || 'true') }}
          upstream_result: ${{ inputs.upstream_result || 'success' }}
      - name: Reserve Health cleanup and diagnostic evidence time
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        run: echo "MESH_HEALTH_DEADLINE_MS=$(( $(date +%s) * 1000 + 23 * 60000 ))" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7.1.0
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/package-lock.json
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'
      - name: Install pinned native inspection toolchain
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        run: python scripts/release/sevenzip.py install
      - name: Install frontend dependencies
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        working-directory: frontend
        run: npm ci
      - name: Check full-source standards and hygiene
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (runner.os == 'Linux') }}
        run: |
          node scripts/validation/standards.mjs
          node scripts/check-repository-hygiene.mjs
      - name: Frontend static checks
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (runner.os == 'Linux') }}
        working-directory: frontend
        run: |
          npm run format:check
          npm run lint
          npm run typecheck
      - name: Audit frontend dependencies
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (runner.os == 'Linux') }}
        working-directory: frontend
        run: npm run audit:ci

      - name: Validate public help and MCP
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        run: |
          npm ci --prefix tools/help --ignore-scripts
          node --test tools/help/*.test.mjs

      - name: Audit help dependencies
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (runner.os == 'Linux') }}
        run: npm audit --prefix tools/help --audit-level=high

      - name: Frontend unit tests and coverage
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (runner.os == 'Linux') }}
        working-directory: frontend
        run: npm run test:coverage

      - name: Seal browser unit line map from this run
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (runner.os == 'Linux') }}
        run: node scripts/ci/unit-coverage-artifact.mjs seal frontend/coverage/lcov.info target/ui-unit-coverage

      - name: Upload browser unit line map
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (runner.os == 'Linux') }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: ui-unit-coverage-${{ github.sha }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: target/ui-unit-coverage/
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7

      - name: Upload frontend coverage
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (always() && matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest') }}
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: frontend-coverage-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: frontend/coverage/
          if-no-files-found: warn

      - name: Delivery and AI eval smoke
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest') }}
        run: |
          make eval-smoke
          node --test scripts/test-ai-eval.mjs

      - name: Install Rust for diagnostic Cargo fixtures
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - name: Native release inspection regression
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (runner.os == 'Linux') }}
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y nsis

      - name: Verify native NSIS payload equivalence
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (runner.os == 'Linux') }}
        run: python scripts/release/test_native_nsis.py -v

      - name: Diagnostic and release gate regressions (all platforms)
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          node scripts/validation/stage.mjs diagnostics --profile shared --deadline "$MESH_HEALTH_DEADLINE_MS" --result tmp/health-diagnostics.json -- node --test --test-reporter=spec --test-reporter-destination=stdout --test-reporter=./scripts/diagnostics/node-test-progress.mjs --test-reporter-destination=target/validation/health-progress.jsonl scripts/diagnostics/*.test.mjs

      - name: Preserve diagnostic execution evidence
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (always()) }}
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: health-diagnostics-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: |
            tmp/health-diagnostics.json
            target/validation/
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14

      - name: Build retention safeguards (all platforms)
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        run: python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p test_build_retention.py -v

# Finishing a Development Branch

## Overview

Guide completion of development work by presenting clear options and handling chosen workflow.

**Core principle:** Verify tests → Present options → Execute choice → Clean up.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the finishing-a-development-branch skill to complete this work."

## The Process

### Step 1: Verify Tests

**Before presenting options, verify tests pass:**

```bash
# Run project's test suite
npm test / cargo test / pytest / go test ./...
```

**If tests fail:**
```
Tests failing (<N> failures). Must fix before completing:

[Show failures]

Cannot proceed with merge/PR until tests pass.

# Module Ownership and Reuse

This is the implementation ownership map for maintaining Mesh Talk and assigning
parallel work. Use it to locate the owner of a decision before adding another
implementation. Network semantics and configuration belong to the
[communication architecture](network-design-reference.md); this document defines
where those decisions live in code and how to change them safely.

The [canonical glossary](../CONTEXT.md) defines domain concepts;
[DDD conventions](domain-design.md) define modeling terms and identifier mappings.
The layers and owners below are implementation responsibilities, not declarations
that every module or crate is a separate DDD bounded context.

## 1. Dependency direction

| Layer                                       | Owns                                                                                          | Depends on                                              | Must delegate                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Protocol core: `crates/mesh-talk-core`      | Identity, membership, encryption, admission, persistence, transport and delivery correctness  | Rust libraries and its internal modules                 | Native platform behavior and presentation                            |
| Desktop host: `src-tauri`                   | Session/runtime installation, OS integration, settings persistence, authorized IPC adaptation | Core public exports                                     | Wire validation, cryptographic authority and delivery state machines |
| Typed IPC: `frontend/src/lib/api`           | Command names, payload shapes, typed results                                                  | Shared types, Tauri APIs and sibling adapters           | UI stores, React features and business decisions                     |
| Application stores: `frontend/src/store`    | Reactive state, owner-scoped work, optimistic intents, cache transitions                      | Typed adapters and shared projections                   | Core authority and feature rendering                                 |
| Feature modules: `frontend/src/features`    | User interaction and composition                                                              | Stores, typed adapters, shared models and UI primitives | Reimplementation of identity, policy or delivery rules               |
| UI primitives: `frontend/src/components/ui` | Accessible visual controls                                                                    | React/Radix and styling helpers                         | Session lifecycle and protocol policy                                |

The bot integration service in `crates/mesh-talk-integrations` depends on the core
and host-supplied admission ports. It owns grants, bounded metadata audit and
private IPC and its fixed-route loopback HTTP adapter; `crates/mesh-talk-mcp` owns SDK/stdio translation only. Core
`node/outgoing_message.rs` owns retry-safe event acceptance and sender-state WAL
recovery. Desktop `src-tauri/src/integrations.rs` binds exact-session leases and
graceful listener retirement. `integrations/local_access.rs` owns serialized
settings/startup control and the single desktop service handle;
`integrations/instructions.rs` owns only the marked user-level bootstrap file.
Both transports share one integration service/registry and core sending path.
`http.rs` owns public static discovery, request limits and fixed scoped routes;
request schemas derive from the existing models. The Agent access settings UI uses
the shared save coordinator and an explicit-owner typed adapter. See
[desktop local access](bot-integrations.md#desktop-local-agent-access).

The local access owner persists absolute authorization deadlines and preserves
them across service retries and session/runtime restarts. Only an explicitly
verified enable, duration extension or renewal can extend authority. The shared
integration grant authorizer checks expiry again at core acceptance. The desktop
activity view uses the existing registry's bounded content-free send projection:
read the live service registry while its supervisor exists, and open the saved
registry only after its writer has stopped under the same controller serialization.
The UI never creates a second grant-store owner or attributes a shared credential
to a particular AI application. See [authorization lifetime](bot-integrations.md#lifecycle-and-authority).

The headless CLI uses the core directly. A protocol change should not require
Tauri; a presentation change should not alter the wire protocol. Not every helper
in `lib/` is pure: `theme.ts`, for example, owns reactive appearance effects. Use
specific modules rather than assuming the directory name implies purity.

The existing API facade remains stable. Its settings owner resolver is composed
at the application seam; adapters never import stores. ESLint enforces that rule
for alias imports and relative imports at any nesting depth. The auth store uses
low-level adapters to avoid recreating the facade/settings/auth runtime cycle.

ESLint also rejects static imports of rendering modules (`components/` and
`features/`) from stores and IPC adapters, including type-only imports and nested
relative paths. Shared presence vocabulary lives in `lib/presence.ts`; identity
controls re-export it for compatibility. Stores own evidence expiry and state
transitions; controls own visual mapping. These checks cover direct static
dependencies, not transitive dependencies or dynamic imports.

# Writing Plans

## Overview

Write comprehensive implementation plans assuming the engineer has zero context for our codebase and questionable taste. Document everything they need to know: which files to touch for each task, code, testing, docs they might need to check, how to test it. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

Assume they are a skilled developer, but know almost nothing about our toolset or problem domain. Assume they don't know good test design very well.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

**Context:** This should be run in a dedicated worktree (created by brainstorming skill).

**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
- (User preferences for plan location override this default)

## Scope Check

If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.

## File Structure

Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.

- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
- In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.

This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.

## Bite-Sized Task Granularity

**Each step is one action (2-5 minutes):**
- "Write the failing test" - step
- "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
- "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
- "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
- "Commit" - step

## Plan Document Header

**Every plan MUST start with this header:**

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

---
```

### Locator.press

Source: https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/v1.64.1/docs/src/api/class-locator.md

Focuses the matching element and presses a combination of the keys. It focuses the element and then uses Keyboard.down and Keyboard.up to simulate the key press.

```APIDOC
## Locator.press

### Description
Focuses the matching element and presses a combination of the keys. Focuses the element, and then uses `Keyboard.down` and `Keyboard.up`.

### Method
Locator.press

### Parameters
#### Arguments
- **key** (string) - Required - Name of the key to press or a character to generate, such as `ArrowLeft` or `a`.

#### Options
- **delay** (float) - Optional - Time to wait between `keydown` and `keyup` in milliseconds. Defaults to 0.
- **noWaitAfter** - Optional - (see input-no-wait-after)
- **timeout** - Optional - (see input-timeout)
- **signal** - Optional - (see input-signal)

### Since
v1.14

### Request Example
```js
await page.getByRole('textbox').press('Backspace');
```

```java
page.getByRole(AriaRole.TEXTBOX).press("Backspace");
```

```python async
await page.get_by_role("textbox").press("Backspace")
```

```python sync
page.get_by_role("textbox").press("Backspace")
```

```csharp
await page.GetByRole(AriaRole.Textbox).PressAsync("Backspace");
```
```

--------------------------------

### Press keys and shortcuts in JavaScript

Source: https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/v1.64.1/docs/src/input.md

Focuses the target locator and emits single keystrokes or shortcut combinations like Enter, Control+ArrowRight, or $. Accepts keyboardEvent.key logical names.

```js
// Hit Enter
await page.getByText('Submit').press('Enter');

// Dispatch Control+Right
await page.getByRole('textbox').press('Control+ArrowRight');

// Press $ sign on keyboard
await page.getByRole('textbox').press('$');
```

--------------------------------

### Press a key on a locator in JavaScript

Source: https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/v1.64.1/docs/src/api/class-locator.md

Focuses the matching element and presses the given key combination. Use `page.getByRole('textbox')` to target the element before calling `press`.

```javascript
await page.getByRole('textbox').press('Backspace');
```

--------------------------------

### Locator.pressSequentially

Source: https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/v1.64.1/docs/src/api/class-locator.md

Focuses the element, and then sends a keydown, keypress/input, and keyup event for each character in the text. In most cases, you should use Locator.fill instead; only use this method if there is special keyboard handling on the page. To press a special key like Control or ArrowDown, use Locator.press.

```APIDOC
## Locator.pressSequentially

### Description
Focuses the element, and then sends a `keydown`, `keypress`/`input`, and `keyup` event for each character in the text. In most cases, you should use `Locator.fill` instead; you only need to press keys one by one if there is special keyboard handling on the page. To press a special key, like `Control` or `ArrowDown`, use `Locator.press`.

### Method
async method

### Parameters
#### Arguments
- **text** (string) - Required - String of characters to sequentially press into a focused element.

#### Options
- **delay** (float) - Optional - Time to wait between key presses in milliseconds. Defaults to 0.
- **noWaitAfter** - Optional
- **timeout** - Optional
- **signal** - Optional

### Request Example

```js
await locator.pressSequentially('Hello'); // Types instantly
await locator.pressSequentially('World', { delay: 100 }); // Types slower, like a user
```

```java
locator.pressSequentially("Hello"); // Types instantly
locator.pressSequentially("World", new Locator.pressSequentiallyOptions().setDelay(100)); // Types slower, like a user
```

```python async
await locator.press_sequentially("hello") # types instantly
await locator.press_sequentially("world", delay=100) # types slower, like a user
```

```python sync
locator.press_sequentially("hello") # types instantly
locator.press_sequentially("world", delay=100) # types slower, like a user
```

```csharp
await locator.PressSequentiallyAsync("Hello"); // Types instantly
await locator.PressSequentiallyAsync("World", new() { Delay = 100 }); // Types slower, like a user
```

An example of typing into a text field and then submitting the form:

```js
const locator = page.getByLabel('Password');
await locator.pressSequentially('my password');
await locator.press('Enter');
```

```java
Locator locator = page.getByLabel("Password");
locator.pressSequentially("my password");
locator.press("Enter");
```

```python async
locator = page.get_by_label("Password")
await locator.press_sequentially("my password")
await locator.press("Enter")
```

```python sync
locator = page.get_by_label("Password")
locator.press_sequentially("my password")
locator.press("Enter")
```

```csharp
var locator = page.GetByLabel("Password");
await locator.PressSequentiallyAsync("my password");
await locator.PressAsync("Enter");
```
```

--------------------------------

### Locator > async method: Locator.press

Source: https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/v1.64.1/docs/src/api/class-locator.md

Focuses the matching element and presses a combination of the keys.

# labali-git-auto-commit-rewrite

## NEVER

- **Never fabricate diff content** or invent changes not present in `git diff` output — a fabricated commit message is worse than no message; it destroys trust in git history.
- **Never amend a previous commit** — always create a new commit. Amending rewrites history and can silently overwrite commits that others (or hooks) have already acted on.
- **Never use `--no-verify`** to bypass pre-commit hooks — the hooks are the project's safety net; bypassing them defeats their purpose and masks real issues.
- **Never write a body that only lists filenames** — `- update core.ts` tells nothing; name the intent behind the change, not the file that changed.

## Commit Type Selection

| Type | When to use |
|------|-------------|
| `feat` | New capability or behavior visible to users/agents |
| `fix` | Corrects wrong behavior (not just wrong output) |
| `docs` | Documentation, examples, references only — no behavior change |
| `chore` | Housekeeping: structure, config, scripts, CI — no behavior change |
| `refactor` | Code restructure with no behavior change |
| `improve` | Meaningful enhancement to existing behavior (not a new feature, not a bug fix) |
| `perf` | Performance improvement |
| `test` | Test additions or changes only |

**Scope selection:** use a scope when the change is confined to one clear subsystem — `fix(browser): ...`, `feat(skill): ...`. Omit scope for cross-cutting changes that span multiple subsystems.

**When types conflict:** if a commit spans both a behavior change and a structural change, use the behavior-change type (`feat`/`fix`/`improve`) — structural changes are secondary to their purpose. If the two concerns are truly independent, split into two commits.

## Execution Contract

1. Inspect working tree changes (`git status --short`, `git diff --name-status`) before writing message.
2. Before writing the subject, determine: is this a behavior change (`feat`/`fix`/`improve`) or a structural change (`docs`/`chore`/`refactor`)? This choice drives the type.
   Generate a commit message that is both clear and elegant:
   - Subject format: `<type>(<scope>): <subject>` or `<type>: <subject>`
   - Subject is concise, action-oriented, and specific to the dominant change set.
   - Body contains 2-6 bullet points, each tied to real grouped changes from diff.
   - Avoid vague wording like only `update`/`align` when multiple meaningful changes exist.
   - **MANDATORY — load `examples/good.md` before writing the message** to calibrate quality. Load `examples/anti-pattern.md` if the draft message feels vague or generic.
3. Stage all changes with `git add -A`.
4. Commit once with the generated subject and body. The commit command MUST be prefixed with `LABALI_SKILL_COMMIT=1` so the repository's pre-commit hook recognizes it as skill-authorized:
   ```bash
   LABALI_SKILL_COMMIT=1 git commit -m "..."
   ```
5. MUST run `<skill_base_dir>/scripts/clean_commit.sh` immediately after commit (non-optional).
   The skill base directory is provided in the `Base directory for this skill:` line at the top of the invocation header.
   `clean_commit.sh` may rewrite the subject — read the final hash and subject from its output, not from the original commit.

## Message Quality Rules

- Body bullets must reflect actual file-level intent, not generic placeholders.
- Prefer aggregate summaries when many files changed, then include concrete sub-actions in body.

## Failure Handling

- If repository is not a Git repo, fail fast with explicit message.
- If there are no changes to commit, return `No changes to commit.`.

## Resources

| When | Must load | Do NOT load |
|------|-----------|-------------|
| Always — before writing the message | `examples/good.md` | `examples/anti-pattern.md` |
| Draft feels vague, generic, or uncertain | `examples/anti-pattern.md` | — |

# Good Commit Message Examples

These examples demonstrate the target quality for commit messages generated by this skill.

---

## Example 1 — Feature with clear scope

```
feat(skill): add license and compatibility fields to all SKILL.md frontmatter
```

**Why it works:**
- Subject is specific and action-oriented, under 72 chars
- Body bullets map to real grouped changes, not generic "update files"
- Scope `(skill)` accurately signals the affected area

---

## Example 2 — Docs restructure

```
docs: restructure standards into docs/ and unify AI entry points

- move DEVELOPMENT.md sections into docs/skill-authoring.md,
  docs/conventions.md, docs/testing.md, docs/workflow.md
- replace CLAUDE.md body with pointer to AGENTS.md
- add Quick Links table in AGENTS.md for per-task doc loading
- keep DEVELOPMENT.md as overview only
```

**Why it works:**
- Type `docs` is correct for non-code changes
- Body explains the reorganization by action, not by file list
- "keep DEVELOPMENT.md as overview only" captures the constraint decision

---

## Example 3 — Bug fix with concise body

```
fix(browser): handle stale CDP connection on cold Chrome start

- detect empty tab list on connect and retry with 2s delay (max 3 times)
- surface actionable error when port is open but Chrome is not ready
- add test fixture for cold-start scenario
```

**Why it works:**
- Subject names the exact symptom, not just "fix bug"

# Mesh Talk: Network Topology and Communication Architecture

This document defines the network architecture and development principles for Mesh Talk's discovery, direct communication, post-office custody, federation, group recovery, file delivery, calls and linked devices. It combines the product intent, current implementation contracts, concrete topology examples and the limits of available evidence.

It is the starting point for evaluating whether a change preserves the agreed communication model. [Architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md) owns the broader protocol and cryptographic reference; the [topology guide](network-topologies.md) provides a compact switch and diagram overview. Operator commands belong in the linked deployment guides.

**Status vocabulary:** **Implemented** means a code path exists under stated conditions. **Configured** means endpoints, permissions or trust must be supplied. **Verified** means a named test observed the specified outcome. **Conditional** names an environmental dependency. **Future** is an explicit extension, not a current promise. A normative statement below describes an invariant to preserve; it does not establish that every topology has passed a physical test.

## Reading paths

- **Evaluate the overall design:** sections 1, 3, 4 and 6.
- **Implement or refactor a feature:** sections 2, 5, 8 and 10.
- **Deploy relays or investigate reachability:** sections 4, 6 and 7, then the operator guides.
- **Assess completeness and evidence:** section 9 and its acceptance boundaries.

## 1. Purpose and boundary

### Product intent and background

Mesh Talk is a local-first conversation system with local identity, authenticated peer connections and end-to-end encrypted content. A local network must remain useful without a post office or vendor-operated account service. A directly routed connection, including Tailscale or EasyTier, extends which application endpoints can communicate. A peer-operated post office adds temporary encrypted custody and, when configured as a bridge, introduces consenting participants and reconciles opaque mail with trusted equal relays.

The desired user experience is that reachable, permitted participants can discover one another and communicate without choosing a global hub. The implementation must still preserve the distinctions between network reachability, device identity, visibility, conversation authority and delivery confirmation.

A client connected to a remote post office can **join that post office's Mesh Talk network**: it can discover eligible registered participants and communicate through the relay. This is application-level participation. It does not install IP routes to every remote machine, forward Ethernet multicast, grant group membership or export all of the client's LAN neighbors.

### Network handoff

Discovery observes interface identities/addresses every two seconds and wakes
existing gated producers after changes, while retaining the 30-second multicast
join retry. Queue replay and authenticated receipts remain owned by the delivery
runtime. Network-namespace handoff acceptance and its limits are maintained in
[routed discovery](routed-network-discovery.md#network-changes-and-recovery).
Physical Wi-Fi/hotspot latency remains a separate hardware acceptance boundary.

### Managed discovery ports

Desktop discovery uses UDP 47474. Every managed post office uses dedicated UDP
47478 and shared LAN UDP 47474, regardless of platform or host. Installers reject
other service discovery ports before modifying installation state. Routed VPN
inventories supply host addresses; desktops probe both role ports within the
existing candidate budget. Managed post offices use main TCP 47479; desktops choose and attempt to reuse
their TCP port. Signed discovery advertises the applicable TCP port;
port numbers and VPN membership never establish identity or authority. Raw CLI
custom-port overrides remain available for isolated tests and explicit endpoints,
not automatic managed discovery. See [routed setup](routed-network-discovery.md).

# Mesh-Talk Architecture

A decentralized, end-to-end-encrypted messenger. **Tauri** desktop shell, **Rust**
backend, **React + TypeScript** frontend. No vendor-operated server: LAN peers
discover each other over signed UDP **multicast** (group `224.0.0.167`, port
47474), connect directly over a Noise-encrypted TCP
channel, and store messages as an append-only, hash-linked **event log** that syncs CRDT-style.
When a peer is offline, a peer-operated **post office** node stores-and-forwards the (still-encrypted)
events. Existing routed networks can supply optional peer discovery; opted-in
post-office bridges introduce registered peers across sites without merging
their IP subnets. See [routed discovery](routed-network-discovery.md) and
[Network Topology and Communication Architecture](network-design-reference.md)
for cross-module design contracts, illustrated scenarios and development guardrails;
[network topologies](network-topologies.md) provides the compact overview.

> The earlier RSA-contact / plaintext-UDP / TCP-relay _legacy_ stack has been retired;
> this local-first stack is the entire product and lives at `/`. The only retained
> piece outside the node is the auth/session layer (`services/auth_service.rs` + `state.rs`),
> which `login` uses before starting the node.

## 1. Process & layers

See the [module ownership and reuse guide](module-boundaries.md) before assigning
parallel feature work or adding shared business logic. It maps current owners and
feature-local interfaces across the core, desktop host and frontend.

```
React UI ── lib/api/*.ts ──invoke()──▶ Tauri IPC (chat_commands/)
   ▲                                    │
   │ Tauri events                       ▼
   └─────────────── RuntimeEvents ← NodeRuntime (node/runtime.rs)
                                           │ discovery, accept, maintenance
                                           ▼
                                   Node (node/node.rs) — orchestration
        ┌──────────────┬───────────────┬──────────────┬───────┴──────┐
   identity/      transport/        eventlog/       discovery/    postoffice/
   ratchet/       (Noise XX)        (DAG + sync)    (signed UDP)  (elect+relay)
   channel/ dm/
        └────────────── storage/encryption.rs (PBKDF2-600k + AES-256-GCM at rest) ──┘
```

`mesh-talk-core` owns protocol state, network tasks, and encrypted persistence.
The desktop shell composes it using `RuntimeConfig` and `RuntimeEvents` in
`src-tauri/src/commands.rs`. `NodeRuntime::start` remains a compatibility
constructor for SDK callers. The shell owns the session and translates inbound
events to Tauri events; it does not own protocol or wire types. Desktop IPC
commands live in `src-tauri/src/chat_commands/`, grouped by account, messaging,

# Mesh Talk: Network Topology and Communication Architecture

This document defines the network architecture and development principles for Mesh Talk's discovery, direct communication, post-office custody, federation, group recovery, file delivery, calls and linked devices. It combines the product intent, current implementation contracts, concrete topology examples and the limits of available evidence.

It is the starting point for evaluating whether a change preserves the agreed communication model. [Architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md) owns the broader protocol and cryptographic reference; the [topology guide](network-topologies.md) provides a compact switch and diagram overview. Operator commands belong in the linked deployment guides.

**Status vocabulary:** **Implemented** means a code path exists under stated conditions. **Configured** means endpoints, permissions or trust must be supplied. **Verified** means a named test observed the specified outcome. **Conditional** names an environmental dependency. **Future** is an explicit extension, not a current promise. A normative statement below describes an invariant to preserve; it does not establish that every topology has passed a physical test.

## Reading paths

- **Evaluate the overall design:** sections 1, 3, 4 and 6.
- **Implement or refactor a feature:** sections 2, 5, 8 and 10.
- **Deploy relays or investigate reachability:** sections 4, 6 and 7, then the operator guides.
- **Assess completeness and evidence:** section 9 and its acceptance boundaries.

## 1. Purpose and boundary

### Product intent and background

Mesh Talk is a local-first conversation system with local identity, authenticated peer connections and end-to-end encrypted content. A local network must remain useful without a post office or vendor-operated account service. A directly routed connection, including Tailscale or EasyTier, extends which application endpoints can communicate. A peer-operated post office adds temporary encrypted custody and, when configured as a bridge, introduces consenting participants and reconciles opaque mail with trusted equal relays.

The desired user experience is that reachable, permitted participants can discover one another and communicate without choosing a global hub. The implementation must still preserve the distinctions between network reachability, device identity, visibility, conversation authority and delivery confirmation.

A client connected to a remote post office can **join that post office's Mesh Talk network**: it can discover eligible registered participants and communicate through the relay. This is application-level participation. It does not install IP routes to every remote machine, forward Ethernet multicast, grant group membership or export all of the client's LAN neighbors.

### Network handoff

Discovery observes interface identities/addresses every two seconds and wakes
existing gated producers after changes, while retaining the 30-second multicast
join retry. Queue replay and authenticated receipts remain owned by the delivery
runtime. Network-namespace handoff acceptance and its limits are maintained in
[routed discovery](routed-network-discovery.md#network-changes-and-recovery).
Physical Wi-Fi/hotspot latency remains a separate hardware acceptance boundary.

### Managed discovery ports

Desktop discovery uses UDP 47474. Every managed post office uses dedicated UDP
47478 and shared LAN UDP 47474, regardless of platform or host. Installers reject
other service discovery ports before modifying installation state. Routed VPN
inventories supply host addresses; desktops probe both role ports within the
existing candidate budget. Managed post offices use main TCP 47479; desktops choose and attempt to reuse
their TCP port. Signed discovery advertises the applicable TCP port;
port numbers and VPN membership never establish identity or authority. Raw CLI
custom-port overrides remain available for isolated tests and explicit endpoints,
not automatic managed discovery. See [routed setup](routed-network-discovery.md).

# Mesh-Talk Architecture

A decentralized, end-to-end-encrypted messenger. **Tauri** desktop shell, **Rust**
backend, **React + TypeScript** frontend. No vendor-operated server: LAN peers
discover each other over signed UDP **multicast** (group `224.0.0.167`, port
47474), connect directly over a Noise-encrypted TCP
channel, and store messages as an append-only, hash-linked **event log** that syncs CRDT-style.
When a peer is offline, a peer-operated **post office** node stores-and-forwards the (still-encrypted)
events. Existing routed networks can supply optional peer discovery; opted-in
post-office bridges introduce registered peers across sites without merging
their IP subnets. See [routed discovery](routed-network-discovery.md) and
[Network Topology and Communication Architecture](network-design-reference.md)
for cross-module design contracts, illustrated scenarios and development guardrails;
[network topologies](network-topologies.md) provides the compact overview.

> The earlier RSA-contact / plaintext-UDP / TCP-relay _legacy_ stack has been retired;
> this local-first stack is the entire product and lives at `/`. The only retained
> piece outside the node is the auth/session layer (`services/auth_service.rs` + `state.rs`),
> which `login` uses before starting the node.
